Three test stub LanguageModel conformances change their prepare() signature from (input, cache, windowSize:) to (input, cache, state: LMOutput.State?, prefill: PrefillParameters). This tracks an apparent upstream mlx-swift-lm protocol change. The stubs are SwitchSlotLanguageModel (ProviderModelSwitchTests.swift:699), EvictionStubModel (StandaloneEvictionOwnershipTests.swift:34) and NoEvictStubLanguageModel (StartupPreloadTests.swift:885). Each stub returns .tokens(input.text), allocates no weights, and performs no inference.

I found no production code, authorization or attestation path, key handling, wire protocol, cache storage, or plaintext handling change in these units. No threat-model asset or boundary is affected. The unchanged ProviderModelSwitchTests body (model-switch drain, coordinator barrier, rollback, weight-hash freshness) is context only, not part of this diff.

The prefill/state parameters are new to the test fixtures. Any production dependency bump or new prefill/state semantics lives outside the supplied evidence. That includes the effect on KV cache, prefix cache (T-041) or GPU residual data (T-028). Those semantics should be reviewed in whatever change updates the mlx-swift-lm dependency and production LanguageModel conformances, not here. I raise no finding from these test changes.
